Are you motivated by complexity, innovation, and the energy transition? Do you want to contribute to a carbon-neutral future, which ENGIE aims to achieve by 2045? Then ENGIE, leader of the Energy Transition, needs YOU! For the Global Business Unit Supply & Energy Management (S&EM), we are currently looking for a Structurer (M/F/X) . WE OFFER YOU As Structurer An exciting learning journey in a truly international environment, surrounded by top talents and active at the heart of the global energy markets. The opportunity to gain in-depth knowledge of S&EM’s key businesses at the intersection of global energy markets and the energy transition. A rotational path across 2 missions of 18 months each, one based in Brussels and the other in Madrid, offering strong international career prospects. A competitive salary package, with numerous extra-legal benefits: A tax-optimized bonus plan Hospitalization and medical expenses insurance Meal vouchers of 10 EUR with net contribution of 1,09 EUR An attractive retirement plan Green (electric) Company car with load pass for Belgium and neighboring countries or a green alternative through our mobility plan A public transport subscription; our offices are less than 10 minutes from Brussels North station About ENGIE And Supply & Energy Management ENGIE, a global leader in low-carbon energy and services, relies on its Global Business Unit Supply & Energy Management (S&EM) to provide reliable, sustainable, and affordable energy to all its customers. This strategic unit optimizes the Group’s and clients’ production assets and designs tailored energy solutions for its 200,000 professional clients and 15 million consumers. The Global Business Unit Supply & Energy Management leverages ENGIE’s assets to deliver secure and sustainable energy to its BtoB and BtoC customers. It uses its expertise in energy management to provide decarbonized electricity 24/7. Joining Supply & Energy Management means becoming part of a team of over 10,000 passionate experts spread across 20 countries, all united by a shared mission: shaping a greener and more efficient energy future. Together, we push the boundaries of innovation to deliver decarbonized energy 24/7. Join us and be part of those shaping the energy of tomorrow! 🚀 Join ENGIE’s Structuring Program in Supply & Energy Management Our Structuring Program in the Global Business Unit Supply & Energy Management is designed to attract talents with a high potential to grow a career at ENGIE, while contributing to a truly diverse and inclusive culture. ⭐ Why join our Structuring Program? Embark on a thrilling learning journey: work in a truly international environment, surrounded by top talents, and in one of the top companies active in the global energy markets. Gain in-depth knowledge of S&EM’s key businesses at the intersection of global energy markets and the energy transition. Develop strong business skills: work on concrete and impactful projects and transactions, from development to execution, with access to best in class analytics, and some of the most advanced data and systems in the industry. Rotate across teams and geographies: gain exposure to varied and passionate teams across different countries, providing unique international career prospects. Accelerated development: benefit from a highly collaborative culture and access to a network of inspiring leaders. Permanent contract from your first mission and a guaranteed position at the end of the program within S&EM or ENGIE Group. YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES AS Structurer The energy landscape is evolving rapidly, driven by renewables, electrification, new flexible and decentralized technologies (batteries, electric boilers, etc.), geopolitics, and the urgent need for decarbonized, reliable, and affordable energy. Those that know how to embrace this increase in complexity will thrive. We are therefore looking to reinforce our teams with highly-motivated and talented structurers able to leverage complexity into new business opportunities. You will be part of the S&EM’s energy structuring team and learn from top individuals across 2 missions of 18 months each: one based in Brussels and the other based in Madrid. As a structurer you are accountable for the transformation of client needs into transactable solutions. During your program, you will learn to: Shape business opportunities to find the sweet spot between client needs, our risk appetite and our expected return. Identify and price some key risks; market, credit, regulation, operations,… Identify and assess all value pockets of business opportunities. Design and negotiate deals and contracts, in collaboration with legal and support teams. Work together with very diverse profiles (sales, traders, quants, risk managers, legal, etc.). You will learn about the global energy markets, Power Purchase Agreements (PPA) for renewable assets, Flexibility Purchase Agreements (FPA) for batteries, hedging through derivatives (power and cross-commodity options, fixed-for-floating swaps,… ), decarbonized supply offers and more. You will work on impactful business cases to scale up S&EM’s commercial offering and improve our risk management capabilities , such as in 24/7 carbon free energy, co-location of renewable assets and batteries. YOUR PROFILE AS Structurer What Do We Expect From You To make a tangible contribution to the development of the business of the structuring team to which you are part of. We expect you not only to learn, but also to deliver. Your ability to deliver will be a key differentiator. Therefore we are looking for: Master's degree in engineering, Business, Management or a similar field. You have 5-7 years of relevant experience (energy, finance, consultancy,… ). You are eager to learn new skills, curious and ready to be trained. You are fluent in English, any other language, in particular French, Spanish, Dutch and/or German is a strong plus. You are motivated by an international career. You are motivated by the intellectual challenge of putting together high added value deals, you like complexity, and are hands on. Proactive, reliable and results oriented. High standards and attention to details and you demonstrate soundness, discernment, and sharpness in judgment and a drive to excel. Highly inquisitive, interested in the world, and you enjoy understanding and solving complex problems. Strong communication skills and able to influence through non-hierarchical lines and multi-disciplinary working teams. Willing to take up responsibility and accountability early on. Long-term interest in building a career in a strategic, international environment. A giver, not a taker: you truly believe in elevating yourself and your team through generous collaboration. Truly seeking constant self-improvement and growth. Our Recruitment Process Selection process – Step 1: Short pre-screener conversation in teams with the Talent Acquisition Partner Selection process – Step 2: HR in-depth interview on-site / in teams with the Talent Acquisition Partner Selection process – Step 3: Business interviews on-site with your future managers Selection process – Step 4: Job offer Research shows that men apply when they meet 60% of the requirements while women only apply when they are convinced they meet 100% (by Sheryl Sandberg's Lean In) . Don’t let that hold you back – we’d love to hear from you! More About Us ENGIE is committed to promote Equal Opportunity employment. We pro-actively foster an inclusive environment that not only embraces but celebrates diversity. Our goal is for all employees to experience a real sense of belonging. We aim to provide them with a safe and inclusive working environment in which they feel empowered to thrive and excel. At ENGIE, every talent has a role to play in accelerating the energy transition. Make a difference and enjoy a fulfilling professional experience. Take on exciting challenges and build a career path that reflects who you are. Join us and be part of the adventure of the century! review_candidates.description: Automated detection can find vessels, but cannot always tell you which vessel it is. When a contact appears in a satellite image with no matching AIS, when an identity has been spoofed or duplicated, when a name and IMO do not agree, or when the models simply return low confidence, a human analyst has to resolve it. As an OSINT Analyst on Kpler's Maritime Domain Awareness team, you are the adjudication layer behind the machine. You take the detections that automated identification cannot confidently resolve and attach an identity to them: name, IMO, owner, operator, and flag, with the evidence and the confidence to stand behind it. You investigate dark vessels, AIS gaps, GNSS spoofing, and identity manipulation, and you reconstruct the ownership and behaviour that explains what a vessel is really doing. Your work does two things at once. It makes Kpler's unified vessel record more complete and more trusted for the analysts, compliance desks, and government users who depend on it. And it creates the labelled ground truth that makes the detection models better, so the routine cases keep shrinking and human attention stays on the genuinely hard ones. Mission Adjudicate the identifications that automated detection cannot resolve: attach a verified identity to dark, spoofed, or low-confidence contacts, with sourced evidence and an explicit confidence level. Investigate identity manipulation and evasion: AIS gaps and dark periods, GNSS and position spoofing, duplicated or borrowed MMSI, name and flag changes, and vessel substitution. Apply open-source intelligence tradecraft: interpret satellite and optical imagery, work ship-photo databases and vessel registries, corporate and beneficial-ownership records, port-state and terminal records, classification and insurance sources, and open reporting. Reconstruct pattern-of-life and ownership-over-time, building the history that turns a single detection into an explained vessel. Produce structured identification records with clear provenance: every conclusion traceable to its sources, confidence stated plainly, and reporting language disciplined and defensible. Feed the model-improvement loop: return ground truth and edge cases to the data science team, and help define where automation should focus next. Uphold sourcing and data-integrity standards across the team, keeping the record accurate, current, and trusted. Essential Experience & Background 3+ years in intelligence, investigations, maritime analysis, or a related open-source (OSINT) research discipline, with a track record of turning fragmentary evidence into defensible conclusions. Working knowledge of the maritime domain: vessel types and particulars, AIS, registries, flag and ownership structures, and shipping operations. Genuine OSINT tradecraft: source discovery and evaluation, cross-referencing across independent sources, and disciplined handling of uncertainty and provenance. Confidence interpreting imagery (satellite, optical, and ideally SAR) well enough to reason about what a detection is showing. Meticulous, evidence-led documentation and clear written assessments, with careful use of confidence and caveat language. Desirable Familiarity with sanctions, trade compliance, and evasion typologies (shadow-fleet behaviour, ship-to-ship transfers, chokepoint activity). Experience contributing labelled data or ground truth to machine-learning workflows, or working alongside a data science team. GIS and geospatial tooling, and comfort with large datasets. Additional languages relevant to major shipping and registry jurisdictions.
